title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
metaDescription: Classic chocolate chip cookies with crispy edges and a soft, chewy center — the everyday recipe that never needs replacing.
author: Laura Bennett
keywords: chocolate chip cookies, classic cookie recipe, chewy cookies

steps.name: Mix dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk together flour, baking soda and salt in a bowl. Set aside.

steps.name: Cream the butter and sugars
steps.text: In a large bowl, beat the softened butter with both sugars until light and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes.

steps.name: Add eggs and vanilla
steps.text: Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, until fully combined.

steps.name: Combine and add chips
steps.text: Gradually mix in the dry ingredients until just combined — don't overmix. Fold in the chocolate chips.

steps.name: Bake
steps.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto a lined baking sheet, spaced 2 inches apart. Bake for 9-11 minutes until the edges are golden but the centers still look slightly underdone.

tips.question: Why do my cookies come out flat?
tips.answer: Butter that's too warm or melted spreads too much before the structure sets — make sure it's softened but still cool to the touch, and chill the dough for 30 minutes if your kitchen is warm.

tips.question: Why does the recipe say to underbake slightly?
tips.answer: Cookies continue cooking on the hot baking sheet after they come out of the oven — pulling them when the center still looks a touch underdone is what keeps them chewy instead of crisp all the way through.

tips.question: Can I freeze the dough?
tips.answer: Yes — scoop the dough into balls, freeze on a tray until solid, then transfer to a freezer bag. Bake straight from frozen, adding 1-2 extra minutes.

storyIntro: Every family needs one chocolate chip cookie recipe that just works, without needing browned butter or an overnight chill — this is that recipe.
Crispy edges, chewy centers, and a dough that comes together in one bowl in about 15 minutes.
storyNote: Pull the cookies while the centers still look slightly underdone — carryover heat on the hot pan finishes them without drying them out.
